data: View Project on GitHub The Kevinbot P2 Board is a Parallax Propeller 2 Edge Breakout Board catered for robotics use. Originally designed only for use in Kevinbot v3, the board can be used for any P2-based robotics project.

data.specifications#Specifications: Compatible with standard P2 Edge (will not work with the 32 MB option) Prop-Plug Programming Interface 32 Servo Outputs Four One-Wire Ports Four I2C Ports One Serial UART Port One RSL (Status Light) Port Two Voltmeters (1v ~ 33v) One Level-Shifted WS281X(b) port Four 2x6 Way P2 accessory headers Internal and External Error Buzzer Reset Button and External Reset button port Internal DS18b20 thermometer Fully Open Source Design

data.1-p2-edge-socket#1. P2 Edge Socket:
Parallax Propeller 2 Socket (P2-EC)
Not compatible with 32MB RAM upgrade (P2-EC32MB)
data.10-i2c-ports#10. I2C Ports:
Four I2C Ports on a common bus
Refer to Pin Mappings for the internal connections
5v, 3.3v, SDA, SCL, GND starting from the PropPlug side
Do not mix-and-match any of the 3.3v rails. They have the same voltage, but connecting them may result in noisy analog inputs.
data.11-one-wire-ports#11. One-Wire Ports:
4 One-Wire Ports on a common bus
Refer to Pin Mappings for the internal connections
5v, 3.3v, DATA, GND starting from the PropPlug side
Do not mix-and-match any of the 3.3v rails. They have the same voltage, but connecting them may result in noisy analog inputs.
data.12-led-output-port#12. LED Output Port:
LED Port intended for a single data wire addressable LED segment (such as WS2812b, WS2811, etc…)
Logic level is shifted to the input voltage
data.13-rsl-output-port#13. RSL Output Port:
The RSL port is intended for a robot status light. For example, a light that turns on when motors are enabled
Output Voltage: 5v Max Output Current: 1.3A
data.14-uart-communication-port#14. UART Comm:
This port is intended to be used as a serial communication link between the P2 Board and a main processor like a Raspberry Pi, or another Kevinbot P2 Board. While using this port is entirely optional, it may be required for more complex applications.
Using shielded cable is recommended at higher data rates
data.15-external-reset-button-port#15. Extern: This port is for an external PC-like reset button. A connection between the two pins will result in the CPU restarting.
data.16-external-error-buzzer-port#16. Extern:
This port is for a software-controlled external Piezo Buzzer.
Output Voltage: 5v Max Output Current: 1.3A
data.17-reset-button#17. Reset Button: Pressing the button will result in the CPU and code execution restarting.
data.18-led-indicators#18. LED Indicators:
Indicates power rail statuses and UART port activity.
Light meanings: TX = UART transmitting RX = UART receiving SVO = Servo power rail 3V3 = P2 V24 rail 5V = 5V Input rail
data.19-propplug-programming-interface#19. Pr: Header for programming the P2. Designed for use with a Parallax Prop Plug
data.2-5v-dc-input#2. 5V DC Input:
Maximum Voltage: 5.25v
Uses Phoenix Contact MSTBA style connector
data.20-internal-ds18b20-thermometer#20. Inte: Every Kevinbot P2 Board will have a different serial number identifier for the thermometer. It is required to know the serial number if you have any devices connected to the One-Wire ports
data.21-second-servo-bank#21. Second Servo Ba:
This is the second bank of servo ports (S16 ~ S31) They are connected to a PCA9685 at I2C address 0x41
Each port has a maximum rating of 3A The whole bank has a rating of 6.5A
data.22-first-servo-bank#22. First Servo Bank:
This is the first bank of servo ports (S0 ~ S15) They are connected to a PCA9685 at I2C address 0x40
Each port has a maximum rating of 3A The whole bank has a rating of 6.5A
data.23-ground-test-points#23. Ground test po: These ground points can be invaluable when debugging hardware. Clip your oscilloscope ground to them and debug away!
data.24-battery-input-polyfuses#24. Battery I: These fuses are for the battery voltmeters. They auto-reset after tripped. They should never trip unless the board or P2 is damaged in some way.
data.25-error-buzzer#25. Error Buzzer: This is a piezo buzzer intended for error tones. In the standard Kevinbot code, it will play a startup chime, and continuously beep if an error has occurred.
data.26-error-buzzer-enabler#26. Error Buzzer: This jumper should be installed to enable the internal error buzzer. If the jumper is not installed, the external buzzer port will still be active.
data.27-expansion-connector#27. Expansion con: This connector is reserved for future use. A pinout is provided here
data.3-voltmeter-for-battery-1#3. Voltmeter f:
Do not apply more than 33v to the input, or you will damage the P2.
Uses Phoenix Contact MSTBA style connector
data.4-voltmeter-for-battery-2#4. Voltmeter f:
Do not apply more than 33v to the input, or you will damage the P2.
Uses Phoenix Contact MSTBA style connector
data.5-servo-power-input#5. Servo Power Input:
Power input for the 32 servo ports
Do not exceed 6v on the servo input Uses Phoenix Contact MSTBA style connector
data.6-main-fuse#6. Main fuse: Fuse for 5v rail. Replace it with 3A ATM mini fuse
data.7-servo-fuse#7. Servo fuse:
Fuse for servo rail. Replace it with 15A ATM mini fuse
Current Warning Exceeding these rating may cause overheating of the board traces and/or connectors Servo channel current ratings:
10A Max total current 6.5A Max for each bank of 16 3A Max per channel
data.8-led-power-connector#8. LED Power conne:
Power input LED Output.
The voltage going in will be the WS281X(b) signal level
No current will be drawn from this input
This is not a fused input. Install a fuse on the input side for safe operation
data.9-p2-accessory-ports#9. P2 Accessory Por:
Parallax-compatible P2-EVAL accessory headers. Compatible with all accessories.
Accessory List:
Universal Motor Driver HyperRAM & HyperFlash Add-on HD Audio Add-on set RTC Add-on AV Add-on Serial Host Add-on HUB75 Add-on Board LED Matrix Serial Device Add-on Digital Video Out Goertzel Add-on Mini Proto Add-on Control Add-on Proto Add-on microSD Add-on P2 to MikroBUS Click WX Adapter

data.1-correction#1. Correction:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.
Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.
data.2-warning#2. Warning:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.
Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.
data.3-temporary-ban#3. Temporary Ban:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.
Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.
data.4-permanent-ban#4. Permanent Ban:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.
Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.
data.attribution#Attribution:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.0, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct.html.
Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by Mozilla’s code of conduct enforcement ladder.
For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.
data.enforcement#Enforcement:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at meowmeowahr@gmail.com. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.
All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.
data.enforcement-guidelines#Enforcement Guide: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:
data.enforcement-responsibilities#Enforcement:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.
Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.
data.our-pledge#Our Pledge:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.
We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.
data.our-standards#Our Standards:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:
Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community Examples of unacceptable behavior include:
The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks Public or private harassment Publishing others’ private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting
data.scope#Scope: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

data: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Kevinbot P2 Board! Your contributions, whether in hardware design, documentation, or ideas, help the project grow. Please take a moment to review this guide to make the process easier for everyone.
data.before-submitting-a-bug-report#Before Su: Make sure you’re using the latest KiCAD version (if applicable). Verify the issue isn’t due to configuration or environment issues. Search the bug tracker to see if the issue has already been reported. Gather the following details: Software versions (e.g., KiCAD, P2 Compiler) Reproduction steps or related input/output
data.before-submitting-an-enhancement#Before: Make sure you’re using the latest version. Check the documentation to ensure the feature isn’t already covered. Search the issue tracker for similar suggestions.
data.i-have-a-question#I Have a Question:
Before asking:
Check the Documentation. Search the Issues and Discussions. Still need help?
Open a new topic in Q&A, providing as much context as possible.
data.submitting-a-bug-report#Submitting a Bug:
Sensitive issues (e.g., security bugs) should be reported via email at meowmeowahr@gmail.com.
For all other issues:
Open a GitHub issue. Describe the expected and actual behavior, along with clear reproduction steps. Include the details you gathered earlier.
data.submitting-an-enhancement-suggestion#Sub: Discuss your idea in the Discussions section. Once your idea is clear, open a new issue with: A descriptive title A detailed explanation of the suggestion and expected outcome Why the feature would benefit users
data.ways-to-support-the-project#Ways to Supp:
Even if you don’t have time to contribute directly, you can support us by:
Starring the repository Sharing it on social media Mentioning it in your project’s README

data.general-p2-objects#General P2 Objects:
jm_ds18b20.spin2 A driver can be found here
This will work for interfacing with the single sensor on the board, or external sensors via the One-Wire ports. You can use the One-Wire scanner tool on the Kevinbot v3 GitHub Repo
ka_pca9685.spin2 The driver can be found here
This is the driver for controlling the servo banks. You will need to initialize two instances of the driver to use both banks.
